question: Which statement best describes Block?
options: An inline box flows within a line of text and takes only the space it needs. Links commonly behave this way. It is like a word inside a sentence rather than a separate paragraph. Ordinary inline boxes do not respond to width and height like blocks, so choose a different display mode when you need a sized box.

Flexbox arranges children along one main direction, either a row or a column. It can align items and distribute free space. It is like arranging books on one shelf. Use it for a toolbar, navigation row, or a column of controls when the items mainly follow one direction.

`inline-block` stays in line with neighboring content while accepting width and height. It is like a compact label that sits beside text but still has its own box. It appears in older layouts and is useful for small controls, though Flexbox or Grid often make larger arrangements easier to manage.

A block box normally starts on a new line and takes the available width. Paragraphs and headings commonly behave this way. It is like placing a large box on its own shelf. Width and height can be set, but the exact behavior also depends on the element and its other layout rules.
explanation: A block box normally starts on a new line and takes the available width. Paragraphs and headings commonly behave this way. It is like placing a large box on its own shelf. Width and height can be set, but the exact behavior also depends on the element and its other layout rules.
